chapters.title: Chapter 4: AIS and TIS, the Full Picture of Your Financial Year

lessons.title: Wrong Entry in AIS? How to Submit Feedback

children.text: Aarti, a chartered accountant working in industry in Kolkata, opens her AIS for FY 2025-26 and finds two problems. A ₹1,20,000 interest entry from an FD where she is only the second holder: the money is her mother's, and her mother reports the interest. And a ₹3,00,000 mutual fund redemption that appears twice, pushing her TIS to ₹6,00,000. Left alone, both would flow straight into her pre-filled return.
Unlike Form 26AS, where only the deductor can fix errors, AIS lets you respond directly. That response is called feedback, and using it well is one of the most practical skills in this course.
When to Give Feedback, and When Not To

body.title: Feedback is for wrong information, not inconvenient information

columns.label: Give feedback when
points: The amount or details are wrong
The income belongs to another person
The entry relates to a different financial year
You never had the transaction at all

columns.label: Do not give feedback when
points: The entry is correct but the income is exempt or deductible. Claim that in your return instead.
The entry is correct but you forgot about it. Report it.
You simply do not want the income taxed
The problem is missing TDS credit. That needs the deductor's correction.

body.text: Feedback is not a way to make income disappear. Wrong reporting is taken up with the source for confirmation. If you deny income you actually earned and the bank or registrar confirms its original report, you have created exactly the mismatch you were trying to avoid, and it can lead to verification or a notice.

children.text: Every AIS entry offers a set of standard options. Some categories add customised options specific to that type of information.

body.caption: AIS feedback options and when to use them

cells: Information is correct
The entry is accurate
Your salary entry matches Form 16
Information is not fully correct
The transaction is yours but the amount or details are wrong
Interest reported as ₹48,000 but your bank statement shows ₹43,000
Information relates to other PAN/year
The income belongs to someone else, or to a different financial year
Joint FD interest that belongs to the first holder whose money it is
Information is duplicate/included in other information
The same transaction already appears in another entry
One redemption reported twice, and not removed in TIS
Information is denied
You never had this transaction at all
A property sale in a city you have never owned property in
Customised feedback
An option specific to that information category fits better
Category-specific options, for example on transfers of securities

children.text: on the e-filing portal, go to the
tab and select the financial year.
tile and expand the section with the wrong entry, such as SFT information.
Click the information category, then find the specific entry.
Choose the feedback option and fill in the details it asks for, such as the correct amount, or the other PAN or year.
. You receive a confirmation by email and SMS and can download an acknowledgement.
Go to Feedback History and choose Modify Feedback. There is currently no limit on how many times you can modify feedback.
You can select several transactions and give bulk feedback, though only some options are available in bulk.

Once submitted, your feedback appears alongside the entry, and the modified value is shown next to the value originally reported. The derived value in TIS updates to reflect your feedback, so your pre-filled return uses the corrected figure.

Where your feedback says the source reported wrongly, it is shared with that source for confirmation automatically. This works for information from tax deductors and collectors and from SFT reporting entities. AIS shows the status of that confirmation.

body.title: Aarti's feedback on the joint FD

events.title: Feedback submitted
events.description: She marks the ₹1,20,000 entry as Information relates to other PAN/year and enters her mother's PAN.

events.title: TIS updates
events.description: The derived value for interest from deposits drops by ₹1,20,000. Her pre-filled return now uses the lower figure.

events.title: Shared with the bank
events.description: AIS shows the feedback was shared with the bank for confirmation, with the date.

events.title: Source responds
events.description: The bank accepts or rejects the feedback, and the response appears in AIS. If it rejects, Aarti keeps proof that the deposit was funded by her mother.

body.caption: Aarti's TIS before and after feedback

cells: Interest from deposit
Joint FD interest of ₹1,20,000 relates to another PAN. Her own SBI FD interest of ₹30,000 stays.
Sale of mutual fund units
Second report of the same ₹3,00,000 redemption marked as duplicate

body.text: AIS feedback fixes what the department believes you earned. It does not fix the tax credit you get. For missing or wrong TDS, you still need the deductor to correct its statement.

body.title: Choose the option
body.question: Sameer's AIS shows interest of ₹85,000 from an FD in the joint names of his father and himself. His father funded the FD and is the first holder. Which feedback option fits best?
options: Information is duplicate/included in other information
body.explanation: The transaction exists, so it is not denied, but the income belongs to his father, whose money funded the deposit. Information relates to other PAN/year, with his father's PAN, is the right choice.

body.title: Aarti's derived interest
body.prompt: Before feedback, Aarti's TIS shows interest from deposits of ₹1,50,000, made up of ₹1,20,000 from the joint FD and ₹30,000 from her own SBI FD. After she marks the joint FD entry as relating to another PAN, what should the derived value be?
body.explanation: ₹1,50,000 minus ₹1,20,000 = ₹30,000. Only her own SBI interest remains in the derived value, which is what pre-fills her return.

body.title: Find the button
body.textWithBlank: To give feedback on an AIS entry, click the ___ button in the Feedback column for that entry.
body.explanation: The Feedback column shows an Optional button. Clicking it lets you choose a feedback option and enter details.

body.title: Mohit wants to deny his savings interest
body.scenario: Mohit, an old-regime taxpayer in Chandigarh, sees ₹9,000 of savings account interest from Punjab National Bank in his AIS. A friend tells him savings interest up to ₹10,000 is tax-free, so he plans to mark the entry as Information is denied to keep it out of his return.
body.prompt: Is this the right approach? What should Mohit do instead?
body.modelAnswer: No. The information is correct: the bank did pay him ₹9,000 of interest. Denying it would be false feedback, and the bank would reject it on confirmation. The right approach is to leave the entry as it is, or mark it as correct, and report the ₹9,000 as income in his return. Under the old regime he can then claim the deduction for savings account interest of up to ₹10,000, which brings the taxable amount to zero. Exempt or deductible income is handled in the return, not by disputing correct information in AIS.

body.title: Harsh and the stranger's fees
body.scenario: Remember Harsh from Chapter 3, whose Form 26AS showed ₹3,00,000 of professional fees under section 194J from a Delhi consultancy he never worked with. The same entry appears in his AIS under TDS information.
body.prompt: What feedback should he give, and what will it fix?
body.modelAnswer: He should mark the entry as Information is denied, since he never had any transaction with that consultancy. The feedback removes the ₹3,00,000 from the derived value in his TIS, so it does not pre-fill his return as income. It is shared with the consultancy as the source for confirmation. What it does not do is correct Form 26AS. That still needs the consultancy to file a correction statement fixing the PAN, so Harsh should also contact it using the TAN. He should not claim the ₹30,000 of TDS in his return either way.

body.title: Before you submit feedback
steps: Confirm the entry is actually wrong, not just unexpected or exempt.
Gather proof: bank statements, capital gains statements, deposit receipts or proof that someone else funded the transaction.
Pick the most precise option: not fully correct, other PAN/year, duplicate or denied.
Enter correct values or the other PAN carefully.
Save the acknowledgement and check TIS has updated.
Come back later to check the source's response in AIS.

points: Give AIS feedback only when information is wrong. Exempt or deductible income is handled in your return.
The main options are: correct, not fully correct, relates to other PAN/year, duplicate and denied, plus customised options for some categories.
Click Optional in the Feedback column, choose an option, add details and submit. You can modify feedback any number of times.
Your feedback updates the derived value in TIS, which pre-fills your return.
Feedback on wrong reporting is shared with the source for confirmation, and AIS shows whether it accepted or rejected it.
AIS feedback does not fix TDS credit in Form 26AS. That still needs the deductor's correction.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects the AIS feedback facility as of September 2026. Names, PANs and amounts are illustrative, and options and screens can change. Ownership of income from joint accounts depends on who provided the funds, so consult a chartered accountant for your situation.
